recommended_approach: Use a Mantaflow Gas setup (at minimum: one Fluid **Domain** and one **Flow** emitter) to generate a small plume, then render it with a **Principled Volume** material on the Domain using volume attributes (especially **temperature**) to drive **blackbody emission**. In shading, rely on the Principled Volume node’s built-in support for fire (Blackbody Intensity + Temperature/Temperature Attribute), or use the Volume Info node’s Temperature/Flame outputs to drive a Blackbody/Emission network.

requirements: At least one Domain and one Flow
steps_in_order: Create Flow object(s) to emit gas/smoke/fire
Optional: add Effectors/colliders/force fields to shape motion
Assign a material to the Domain to render density/temperature-driven shading
Bake Cache to generate simulation data for playback/render

blackbody.blackbody_intensity_note: Set to 1 for physically accurate intensity

volume_info_node_outputs_from_docs.density: Scalar density of smoke inside the Fluid Domain
volume_info_node_outputs_from_docs.flame: Scalar density of fire inside the Fluid Domain (Flame output)
volume_info_node_outputs_from_docs.temperature: 0–1 maps to 0–1000 kelvin; can be used for physically-based fire with Blackbody or Principled Volume shaders

warnings: Volume attribute/grid names must match what the shader expects (docs explicitly call out typical names like “density”, “color”, and “temperature”).
Volume Info Temperature output is normalized: values in 0–1 map to 0–1000 kelvin (you may need to account for this in your shader if you expect absolute kelvin values).
Save the blend-file before baking (recommended in the Mantaflow workflow).
Domain must exist before baking; changes to Domain/Flow settings generally require re-baking to take effect.
alternative_approaches: Instead of only Principled Volume, build a custom volume shader by combining Volume Scatter/Absorption/Emission components, and feed volume attributes via Attribute or Volume Info nodes (manual notes this as the path for more control).

Drive fire color via a Blackbody node using Volume Info → Temperature (normalized) into Blackbody, then into a Volume Emission (or into Principled Volume’s emission inputs), rather than relying purely on Principled Volume’s Temperature Attribute field.
